title: Lodestar Payments onramp & hosting criteria discussion
meeting_header: Date: 2028-03-14 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes | Recording: yes
summary: Initial discovery with Lodestar Payments exploring Redwood for a payments-facing assistant. Key constraints: PCI/PII handling, VPC or on-prem options, SOC2 scope, and TTFT for a PLG pilot. Agreed to provide security pack, trial credits, and run latency/cost benchmark with sample workload.
topics: Security: SOC2, PCI, KMS, audit logs
Perf: latency SLOs, batching, KV cache
POC scope: bench with tokenized PM workflow
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we can kick off. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. With me is Thomas, our SE. Lina from success is here too.
[00:10] Priya Nair: Hi Maya, thanks. Quick intro — i'm Priya, cto at Lodestar. We do payment orchestration for marketplaces, lots of card data flows.
[00:18] Omar Haddad: Omar, infra/sre. we'll be looking at network controls and egress.
[00:23] Jules Martin: Jules, product, i'm driving the assistant use cases.
[00:28] Maya Chen: Great. High-level — is this a PLG-first approach? are you aiming for free credits and a quick prototype?
[00:35] Priya Nair: Yes, we want a quick pilot to show product value. time-to-first-token is critical — if engineers can get something live in a day or two that's ideal. But security is non-negotiable: PCI scoping means we can't send raw PAN data to hosted endpoints without tokenization.
[00:50] Thomas Boyd: Understood. We typically recommend the PLG path for prototypes — self-serve API, free credits, sandbox model. For PCI-heavy flows we look at either Dedicated with strict network egress controls or Private (VPC or on-prem) depending on audit requirements.
[01:05] Katerina Voss: Quick q — does Redwood have a PCI attestation or do you rely on customer tokenization?
[01:11] Maya Chen: We don't represent PCI compliance for payments in the hosted tier as a full attestation. Most customers tokenize card data before it reaches the model. For regulated flows, Dedicated or Private is the recommended path so you can control where keys live and integrate KMS/HSM.
[01:26] Jules Martin: K, so for a product demo we can build with tokenized placeholders. For the pilot we might need to validate latency at scale — sub-200ms end-to-end ideally.
[01:36] Thomas Boyd: That helps. We can run a small benchmark simulating your average request size and prefix lengths. Redwood's runtime supports KV cache and continuous batching; these are levers to hit lower p99. For context, our hosted models can hit ~80-180ms p50 for short prompts depending on the model.
[01:54] Priya Nair: Are those numbers with streaming on or off? we need deterministic latencies.
[02:00] Thomas Boyd: Those are non-streaming completions. Streaming adds a bit of headroom but helps perceived latency. Also quantization and model choice are big factors.
[02:10] Omar Haddad: On networking, is VPC peering available for Redwood hosted? we want to avoid public internet from our PCI scope.
[02:18] Maya Chen: We offer Private with VPC peering or an on-prem bundle. Dedicated can also be placed in a customer VPC for some enterprise contracts. We'll share the network topology guide.
[02:27] Katerina Voss: SSO and audit logs — we need SAML, RBAC, and granular audit trails.
[02:33] Lina Park: Yes, we have SAML/SSO, RBAC, and can export audit logs to your SIEM. We'll include sample logs in the security pack.
[02:40] Jules Martin: Good. For the PLG quickstart — credits & sandbox — what's the developer flow?
[02:45] Maya Chen: We give free credits, API keys, and a quickstart repo. Engineers can make their first request in minutes. TTFT commonly is under a few hours for straightforward prototypes.
[02:53] Priya Nair: Any gotchas? auth rotation, key management?
[02:57] Thomas Boyd: Key rotation is through the console and we integrate with KMS providers for Private. For hosted, we recommend short-lived API keys and a secrets manager. We can demo a simple key rotation snippet.
[03:07] [Speaker 1]: "uh" 
[03:10] Maya Chen: (laughs) that's fine.
[03:12] Priya Nair: Walk me through cost model when we scale to 10k calls/day. Latency and cost tradeoffs are relevant.
[03:20] Thomas Boyd: Absolutely — tokens + compute. For hosted we bill per-token with model profiles. For Dedicated you can buy reserved capacity (predictable throughput, lower unit compute cost). For Private it's more an enterprise license + infra. We can run unit-cost estimates if you share workload mix.
[03:36] Omar Haddad: We'll share sample traffic and avg prompt lengths. Expecting many short prompts where prefix caching would help.
[03:42] Thomas Boyd: That's perfect — prefix/KV caching will reduce tokens and compute. Also continuous batching reduces per-token latency when throughput is higher.
[03:51] Jules Martin: We want to keep a fallback if our primary model is rate limited or behind capacity spikes. Does Redwood do automatic fallback?
[03:58] Maya Chen: Yes we have smart routing and fallback policies — routing by latency, cost or region. You can configure automatic fallback to a compatible model variant.
[04:06] Priya Nair: Security docs and SOC2 — can we get those for procurement?
[04:09] Maya Chen: We'll send a security pack: SOC2 summary, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integrations, audit log samples, and a network topology.
[04:17] Katerina Voss: Also need to know data retention and ability to disable logging for specific routes.
[04:22] Thomas Boyd: We support configurable retention and route-level logging toggles. For Private you control retention policies entirely.
[04:28] Jules Martin: Ok what would a minimal POC look like for us?
[04:31] Maya Chen: Typical POC: 1) get PLG credits and sandbox keys 2) implement a tokenized prompt flow in a staging env 3) we run a 24–72 hour benchmark against your workload with our SEs to capture p50/p95/p99 and unit costs 4) collect security review and gap list for Dedicated/Private.
[04:48] Priya Nair: Timeline? we want results within two weeks ideally.
[04:51] Lina Park: We can usually provision credits and a demo project same-day, SE bench run within 3-7 business days, results and security pack within two weeks.
[04:59] Omar Haddad: For the bench run we need to know what infrastructure you use in hosted — cloud regions, hardware.
[05:05] Thomas Boyd: We'll include model performance profiles by region and typical hardware used; for hosted we run on multiple inference instance classes depending on the model. If you want dedicated GPUs we can put together a reserved capacity quote.
[05:18] [08:12] Priya: Are there any customers with similar compliance footprints?
[05:23] Maya Chen: We have fintech customers in Dedicated/Private setups; we'll anonymize references in the security pack.
[05:29] Jules Martin: Are there SDKs? Our frontend team prefers a JS SDK for quick experiments.
[05:33] Maya Chen: Yes — JS, Python, and strongly typed TypeScript SDKs. We'll link repos.
[05:38] Katerina Voss: Encryption — do you allow customer-managed keys?
[05:41] Thomas Boyd: For Private and some dedicated plans yes; hosted supports KMS integrations but customer-managed HSM depends on contract.
[05:48] Priya Nair: For the POC we will not share raw PAN. We'll send tokenized data and a synthetic dataset with card-like fields.
[05:55] Maya Chen: Perfect — that will keep you in hosted PLG for the proof. Then we can scope Dedicated if procurement needs formalized boundaries.
[06:03] Jules Martin: Next steps recap?
[06:05] Maya Chen: I'll send security pack and quickstart repo. We will provision trial credits and API keys. Thomas will run a bench after you share sample traffic. Lina will coordinate scheduling.
[06:16] Priya Nair: Sounds good. Action owners?
[06:19] Maya Chen: Yes — Maya to send docs; Thomas to scope bench; Lina to provision credits; Priya to provide sample payloads.
[06:27] Omar Haddad: Also include a network diagram for VPC peering options.
[06:30] Thomas Boyd: Will do.
[06:32] [Ending chatter and thanks]
[06:40] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with an email and next steps.
